issues.description: changedFiles path comparison may mismatch absolute vs relative shapes
issues.detail: In `isIncluded`, `filename` is the (possibly absolute) path passed in, run through `cleanUrl` and `slash`. But `changedFiles` comes from `VitestGit.findChangedFiles`, whose output shape (typically absolute, slashed) is not normalized at the boundary before `this.changedFiles.includes(filename)`. The data structure here is a flat array used as a set, and the join key is implicit — if git ever returns a path with a different prefix or casing, every file silently drops out of coverage. Make the data structure explicit: normalize both sides to a single canonical form (slash + resolve) and store as a `Set<string>` for O(1) lookup and clearer intent.

issues.description: Array.includes on changedFiles is O(n*m) across all coverage checks
issues.detail: `isIncluded` is called once per candidate file and now does `this.changedFiles.includes(filename)` — linear scan per call. For a large monorepo with hundreds of changed files and thousands of candidates this is needless quadratic work. Pick the right data structure: a `Set<string>` built once in `onTestRunStart`. Pike's rule 5 applies in reverse here — measure — but the fix is so cheap and obvious there's no reason to ship the array form.

issues.description: onTestRunStart hook is wired in three call sites by hand
issues.detail: The same line `await this.coverageProvider?.onTestRunStart?.()` is repeated immediately after `this._testRun.start(...)` in three places in `core.ts`. That's a data/control-flow duplication: 'test run started' is one event, but it's being announced by three callers who must each remember to call the hook. A junior maintainer will add a fourth `_testRun.start` call and forget the hook, and coverage filtering will silently break. Either fold the hook into `_testRun.start` (one event, one announcement) or expose a small helper that pairs them — so the composition is enforced by structure, not by discipline.

issues.description: CLI transform duplicates the boolean-string coercion logic already used elsewhere
issues.detail: The `transform` for `coverage.changed` open-codes `'true'|'yes'|true` / `'false'|'no'|false` recognition. The top-level `--changed` flag has the same semantics; if the coercion isn't already shared, this is the second copy and a future third one is inevitable. Small composable helper: `parseBooleanOrString(value)` — one function, used by both. Data structure: the input is `string | boolean`, the output is `string | boolean`, the rule is uniform; centralize it.

issues.description: Inheritance from test.changed conflated with coverage.changed semantics
issues.detail: `resolveConfig` copies `resolved.changed` into `resolved.coverage.changed` when the latter is undefined, and `onTestRunStart` then branches on `this.options.changed` vs `this.ctx.config.changed` and re-runs git in the first branch. After resolveConfig inheritance, both will normally be set, so the `else if (this.ctx.config.changed)` branch is dead in practice — except when a user explicitly sets `coverage.changed: false` to opt out, in which case `this.ctx.config.changed` is still truthy and the else branch quietly re-enables filtering using `config.related`. Worth pinning down the intended truth table in one place (a small struct of resolved state) rather than two branches reading two different fields.

issues.description: Test file mode changed to executable (0755) for no reason
issues.detail: `test/coverage-test/test/changed.test.ts` had its mode bit flipped from 0644 to 0755 in this diff. TypeScript test files don't need the executable bit; it's almost certainly a stray `chmod +x` from the author's environment. Strip it.

issues.description: changedFiles cache invalidation relies on caller ordering
issues.detail: `onTestRunStart` calls `this.globCache.clear()` after populating `changedFiles`, which is correct — but the cache is keyed only on filename, not on the (filename, changedFiles-set) pair. If a long-lived process ever re-runs with a different `changedFiles` set without going through `onTestRunStart` (watch mode, for instance), stale cache entries decide inclusion. Either key the cache on a tuple, or make the lifecycle of the cache explicit in the data: e.g., reset the Map reference itself in `onTestRunStart`. Composition over discipline.

review.summary: The feature is small and the data flow is mostly straightforward — a `changedFiles` list, computed once at test-run start, intersected with the include glob. Two data-structure choices hurt it: `changedFiles` is an array used as a set (linear `includes` on every candidate file) and the join key between git output and `isIncluded` input is implicit, not normalized at the boundary. The `onTestRunStart` hook is also wired into `core.ts` by repeating the same line at three call sites, which invites future drift; a junior maintainer will eventually add a fourth `_testRun.start` and forget the hook. Strip the duplicated CLI boolean coercion into a shared helper, drop the stray 0755 mode bit on the test file, and pick the right data structure (a `Set` populated once, normalized once) and most of this code becomes self-evident. Verdict: TOO-CLEVER on the hook plumbing, WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE on `changedFiles`; the rest is SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE.
